subject: Post-call: Nabla AI embedding fit proposal & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@nabla.ai>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@nabla.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Nabla AI embedding fit proposal & pilot next steps

Hi Ellen / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and clear next steps so we can get an initial pilot running that validates model fit for your semantic search use case. I kept this tight — call notes + recommended evaluation plan below.

Call highlights
- Data shape: ~1.1B documents, mostly short clinical notes + product descriptions; average doc length ~220 tokens but long-tail up to 5k tokens.
- Current setup: in-house embeddings (768d) + Annoy-based index; customers reporting recall loss on multi-sentence queries and topical drift when new DOC batches are added.
- Key success metrics: improve recall for long queries (Recall@100), raise MRR@10 for clinical QA slices, keep vector-store size growth manageable.
- Constraints: must remain within current S3 storage + vector DB budget during the pilot, and we need to evaluate quantized models due to cost.

Initial model & eval recommendations (provisional)
1) Candidate models to test:
   - rif-embed-large (1024d) — baseline high-dim for improved semantic fidelity
   - rif-embed-large-q4_0 (1024d quantized) — cost tradeoff; watch for regression on clinical QA
   - rif-embed-compact-768 (768d) — latency/size baseline for comparison

2) Benchmarks and metrics to run (we will provide harness):
   - Primary: MRR@10 (clinical QA slice), nDCG@10 (semantic search relevance)
   - Secondary: Recall@100 (long-query recall), cosine similarity distribution, index storage (GB), average per-query latency
   - Drift checks: KS test on embeddings distribution + mean cosine shift by weekly ingest batch (we'll compute p-values and per-dimension variance)

3) Dimensionality / index guidance
   - Expect ~35% index size increase moving 768 -> 1024; recommend experimenting with PCA to 256/384 for the production vector store if we see limited incremental gains in MRR.

4) Pilot scope & timeline
   - Deliverables: sample-run on 200k documents + 5 curated prompt sets (clinical QA, product search, fuzzy-match), dashboard with MRR/nDCG/Recall slices, and regression alerts for quantized variants.
   - Timeline: 2 weeks to run initial harness, 1 week for analysis and recommendations.
   - Ask: approval to ingest the 200k sample and permission to spin up dedicated developer GPUs for runs.

Attachments: I included an example CSV with a small eval subset and a chart of MAP_vs_dimensionality to illustrate expected tradeoffs.

Next steps (clear asks)
- Ellen / Tom: confirm OK for Redwood to run the 200k eval subset (we only need read access to the sample S3 path).
- Redwood (Marissa): prepare harness config and initial model picks by Monday; Rishi to scope quantization risks.
- Schedule: propose Wed 12/2 10:00am PT for a quick sync to review initial results.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mark/ Ellen — quick technical note from the evaluation side. I ran a lightweight synthetic sweep over a 50k subsample while you confirmed access; preliminary numbers attached. High-level takeaways and configuration we recommend for the 200k run: 

Prelim findings (50k synthetic run)
- rif-embed-large (1024d) improved MRR@10 on the clinical QA slice from 0.36 -> 0.49 (absolute +0.13) compared to the current 768d baseline.
- rif-embed-large-q4_0 (quantized) shows a small drop in MRR@10 (~0.03) but keeps Recall@100 roughly steady.
- PCA to 384 retained ~95% of MRR gains; PCA to 256 lost ~8% of MRR on the clinical slice — still better than baseline in most prompts, but depends on slice.

Recommended harness config for 200k run
- Models: [rif-embed-large, rif-embed-large-q4_0, rif-embed-compact-768]
- Dimensionality evaluations: native dims (1024/768) + PCA-384 and PCA-256 for each model
- Prompt sets: clinical_QA_v1 (Ellen's three problem queries included), product_search_v2, fuzzy_match_v1
- Eval metrics: MRR@10, nDCG@10, Recall@100, index_GB_estimate, avg_latency_95p
- Regression policy: flag if MRR@10 drops >0.05 vs baseline on clinical_QA_v1 for quantized models

Quantization risk note (short)
- Risk: 4-bit quantization can cause per-dimension distortion that disproportionately impacts rare clinical tokens/phrases.
- Mitigation: run paired A/B on clinical slices and fallback route in serving (if quantized model triggers regression, fallback to rif-embed-large for clinical QA route).

Next steps from our side
1) Once you share S3 read path, we'll kick off the 200k harness (2x dev GPUs, 5 days compute).
2) We will surface a short one-page risk summary for your regulatory team with explicit acceptance thresholds for quantized variants.
3) We'll send initial dashboards and the first interim report by Thu 12/3 EOD.

-Marissa
